purpose: Publish every package whose current version is untagged (registry publish, git tag, GitHub release) either locally with `callisto release` or from CI through plan, artifact-manifest and execute, using the merged release PR's committed decision as the only release authority. Every effect is checked against the registry, Git remote or GitHub first, so a rerun finishes a partial release without repeating anything.
scope: Local `callisto release`, the hidden CI release subcommands, decision verification and source checks, operation order, registry publish and observation, reruns and receipts, tags and GitHub releases and assets, the managed release PR, `[release]` config, and release error codes.
non_goals: Forges other than GitHub, and publish targets other than crates.io-style Cargo registries, npm and PyPI.
Checking registry credentials before publishing; cargo, npm, twine and gh report their own auth failures.
A workspace lock file; re-observing Git state before every operation guards against concurrent changes.
Persisting execution state between runs; a rerun re-observes providers from scratch.
Apple code signing and notarization of product assets.

api_surface.name: callisto release
api_surface.description: Publishes every untagged package from the current checkout on any branch. With --dry-run it prints the plan and performs no effect.
error_conditions: Workspace needs the CI route: E239.
Missing or unsafe origin push URL: E132.

api_surface.name: callisto release plan (hidden)
api_surface.signature: callisto release plan [--source-root DIR] (--from-release-commit SHA --decision FILE | --package ECOSYSTEM/NAME...) [--orchestration-revision SHA --artifact-repository OWNER/REPO] --out FILE
api_surface.description: Writes a release plan file (JSON, schemaVersion 5) for a detached source checkout. With --from-release-commit it verifies the committed decision file. With --package it derives the roster from a fresh version plan.
error_conditions: [release] present without both orchestration flags: E231.

api_surface.name: callisto release build-python (hidden)
api_surface.signature: callisto release build-python [--source-root DIR] --intent FILE --artifact-dir DIR
api_surface.description: Builds the sdist and wheel of every Python publish in the plan into the directory, without registry credentials.
error_conditions: Plan publishes no Python package: E308.
A build with no wheel or no sdist: E306.

api_surface.name: callisto release artifact-manifest (hidden)
api_surface.signature: callisto release artifact-manifest --intent FILE --artifact-dir DIR [--seal-python] --out FILE
api_surface.description: Hashes one regular file per declared artifact slot and writes the artifact manifest. With --seal-python it also records the name, size and sha256 of every built Python file of the plan.
error_conditions: Plan declares no slots and --seal-python is absent: E219.
--seal-python on a plan that publishes no Python package: E308.
Asset missing, a symlink or not a regular file: E221.

api_surface.name: callisto release execute (hidden)
api_surface.signature: callisto release execute [--source-root DIR] --intent FILE [--artifact-manifest FILE --artifact-dir DIR] --receipt FILE --orchestration-revision SHA
api_surface.description: Validates the plan file against a fresh derivation from the source checkout, runs every operation, and writes the receipt on full success.

api_surface.name: callisto release inspect (hidden)
api_surface.description: Prints a plan, artifact manifest or receipt JSON document without recomputing it.

api_surface.name: callisto release-pr decide | verify | commit-plan
api_surface.signature: release-pr decide --snapshot FILE|JSON|- --repository OWNER/REPO --base-branch B --release-branch R; release-pr verify --decision X --snapshot X [--applied-head SHA]; release-pr commit-plan --base-commit SHA --message M [--out FILE]
api_surface.description: Decides noop, create or update for the managed release PR from a forge snapshot, re-verifies that snapshot, and builds the commit-API file changes from the staged Git index.

api_surface.name: callisto version --emit-decision
api_surface.description: Writes the release decision (package, target version, inclusion reasons) next to the manifest and changelog edits it applies.

api_surface.name: [release] in callisto.toml
api_surface.description: Declares the product package, its GitHub repository, and the binary assets attached to its GitHub release.
error_conditions: No [[release.artifact]], an unqualified package, an unsafe target or asset-name, a duplicate asset-name, or an unsupported profile: E197.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `callisto release` selects every package that has a publish target other than `none` and whose current version has no matching tag, or has a tag on the current commit while any of its operations is not observed already satisfied. For each one it runs the registry publishes, creates the git tag, and creates the GitHub release when `github-release` is a target. A tag on another commit marks the version released without contacting any provider.
When no package qualifies, `callisto release` prints `Nothing to release.` (JSON: `{"nothingToRelease": true}`), exits 0 and runs no command that publishes, pushes or creates anything.
`callisto release` runs on any branch, leaves HEAD on that branch, and records HEAD's commit as both `releaseSourceRevision` and `orchestrationRevision` in the receipt.

`callisto release --dry-run` prints each package as `<ecosystem/name> <version>` with its operations (a table on a colour terminal, `Release plan:` lines otherwise) and performs no effect. This holds on a dirty worktree, without an `origin` remote, and in a workspace that needs the CI route. With `--format json` it prints the plan document, whose `digest` equals the receipt's `intentDigest` from a following `callisto release` on the same state; the document carries a sibling `diagnostics` array (e.g. an artifact owner selected without its product) when derivation raised any, and omits the field otherwise. `release plan`'s JSON output carries the same `diagnostics` array; the `--out` file it writes never does.
Without an `origin` push URL, `--dry-run` prints one stderr note that tag operations are unbound, and `callisto release` fails with E132 before any effect.

A tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore` makes `callisto release` fail with E267 naming a clean worktree and the offending path, before any effect. Ignored files never count.
Repeated `--package <ecosystem/name>` limits the run to the named packages, every distribution of each, and every package that shares a `fixed` or `linked` group with one of them.
A malformed `--package` value fails with `E227` and an unknown package with E102. A duplicate selection, a version whose release is complete, or a package with no publish target fails with E169.

Suppose a selected package has a runtime, optional or peer dependency on a publishable workspace package whose current version is untagged, and that package is not selected. Planning fails with E169 ("select it too") before any effect. A dependency whose current version is already tagged need not be selected.

In a workspace with `[[release.artifact]]` slots or a napi/maturin platform package, `callisto release` fails with `E239` before any effect. The help names `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest` and `release execute`.

On success, text output is `Released N package(s)`, followed by `; receipt saved to <path>` when `--receipt` is given, and JSON output is the receipt. A receipt file is written only to the `--receipt` path, never into the checkout, and an unwritable `--receipt` path fails the run before any effect.

`--format json` output of `release`, `release --dry-run`, `release plan`, `release execute` and `release artifact-manifest` goes through the same envelope every other command's JSON report uses: a top-level `schemaVersion`, `command` (the subcommand name) and `dryRun`, alongside that subcommand's own payload fields unchanged. The intent and artifact-manifest --out files, receipt --receipt file and version --emit-decision file use their durable document shape without command or dryRun wrapper fields.

`release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path>` takes the package and version roster from the decision file committed in that commit. It does not re-run changeset, group, cascade or pre-release selection.

`release plan --from-release-commit` fails with E165 and writes no output file in any of these cases: HEAD is not the given commit; the commit neither adds nor modifies the decision file; it deletes no direct-child changeset `.md` file (nested Markdown files and `README.md` do not count); a claimed package's manifest does not change to its claimed version; a claimed package's changelog is unchanged; an unclaimed manifest version changes; or a claimed package is not found.

A committed decision file whose digest does not match its entries fails with E166. Each target version is parsed using the grammar of its package ecosystem; durable operation IDs, artifact slots and registry observations bound to an operation use that same grammar. Version values remain strings on the wire, and decision schema versions 1 and 2 are accepted; any other version fails with an error naming the version found.

An abbreviated or unknown `--from-release-commit` SHA, a non-40-hex `--orchestration-revision` for a source with `[release]`, or an `--intent` file with a different `schemaVersion` (`E215`, naming found and expected versions) fails before any output file is written or any effect runs.

`release plan` and `release execute` require the source checkout at a detached HEAD and fail with E170 otherwise. `callisto release` accepts an attached HEAD. Every route requires a complete, non-shallow SHA-1 repository and fails with E266 otherwise.

`release execute` re-derives the plan from the source checkout and fails with E124 before any effect when the result differs from the `--intent` file. A change to the decision, source commit, manifests, config, registry binding or origin remote is enough.

Before each operation, the executor re-checks HEAD, worktree cleanliness and the `origin` push URL. A change stops the run before that operation's effect, with E124 for a moved HEAD or remote and E267 for a dirty worktree.

`release plan` for a source with `[release]` requires `--orchestration-revision` and `--artifact-repository` (`E231`). For a source without `[release]` it ignores both flags, prints a notice, and plans zero artifact slots.

`[release].forge-repository` is the only GitHub destination. Planning rejects an `--artifact-repository` that differs from it (`E230`) or from the `origin` GitHub repository (E175). Execution rejects artifact slots that target another repository, and a `[release]` section without it fails planning with E198.

A graph package has one tag, GitHub release draft and publish, however many ecosystems it publishes to. Its tag is created only after all selected registry publishes belonging to its canonical manifests succeed, in every ecosystem a dual Cargo and npm package publishes to, and its GitHub release draft only after its tag. A `[[release.artifact]]` slot's upload follows the product's draft and gates the product's publish even when a different selected package owns the asset, and the product's publish also waits for the tag of that package, which follows its registry publishes, so the release is published only after the draft, every upload and every publish behind them.

A selected package publishes after the selected packages it depends on through runtime, build, optional or dev edges, and waits for the dependency's distribution in the ecosystem of the declaring manifest, so a Cargo dependent follows a dual package's crate and an npm dependent follows its npm package. A dev edge between two packages in the same dependency cycle does not order them, and a runtime, build or optional cycle fails with E104.

An npm package with attached platform packages publishes each platform package with `npm publish <platform-dir>` before publishing the owner package. Operations run one at a time and the first failure stops the run, so an owner package is never published after one of its platform packages fails.

Cargo publish runs `cargo publish --manifest-path <pkg>/Cargo.toml --locked` from the workspace root, adding `--registry <key>` for registries other than crates.io. It runs only after the on-disk version (resolving `version.workspace = true`) equals the planned version and fails with an on-disk version drift error otherwise.

npm publish picks its tool from the workspace that owns the package and runs there. The owner is the nearest directory at or above the package whose `package.json` declares `workspaces` or that has a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, else for a package no workspace declares the nearest directory with a lockfile, else the root; a lockfile beside a package never moves it out of a declared workspace. The `npm view` observation and a publish by directory run in that same directory, so one `.npmrc` governs what is looked for and what is published. A marker that cannot be inspected is an error, not `npm`. `pnpm-workspace.yaml` alone means pnpm. The tools: `pnpm publish --filter=<name> --no-git-checks`, `yarn workspace <name> npm publish`, `bun publish` in the package directory, and otherwise `npm publish --workspace=<name>`. It appends `--tag <label>` for prerelease versions, where the label is the lowercase letters that start the first prerelease identifier (`1.0.0-beta.2` publishes under `beta`), or `next` when there are none or the word is `latest`, and `--access` and `--registry` when set. A stable version takes the registry default tag.

A scoped npm package (`@scope/name`) with no configured access publishes with `--access public`. A configured access value always wins, and an unscoped package with no configured access gets no `--access` flag.

PyPI publish builds with `python3 -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir <temporary directory>` in the package directory, falling back to `python` and failing with E170 when neither is on PATH, and fails with E306 when the build produced no wheel or no sdist for the version. It then runs `twine upload` naming only the built files the index lacks, with `--repository-url` for a configured upload endpoint (a registry's `publish-url`, else its `url`) and never `--skip-existing`. One build serves the preflight and the publish of a run. Every build runs with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set to the release commit's committer time. `release build-python` runs the same build for each Python publish of a plan into `--artifact-dir`.

A `publishConfig.registry` in package.json that does not match the `url` of an npm-kind `[registries]` entry fails with E120. A registry URL that is not `https`, or has userinfo, a query or a fragment, fails with E126. An `origin` push URL that is not HTTPS or `git@` SSH, or that carries credentials, fails with E132. All three fail before any effect.

Cargo observation runs `cargo --config net.retry=0 info NAME@VERSION --registry <name>` from the workspace root, passing `crates-io` for the default. Exit 0 with a matching `version:` line means present, exit 101 with ``could not find `NAME@VERSION` `` means absent, and anything else is indeterminate.

npm observation runs `npm view NAME@VERSION --json --fetch-retries=0`, with `--registry` when configured. Exit 0 with output means present. A failure whose npm error code is E404, read from the JSON error body on stdout or else from the `code` line on stderr, means absent. Exit 0 with no output, and any other failure, leave the observation indeterminate and are never read as absence.

PyPI observation fetches `<index>/<normalized-name>/` (the registry's `url`, default `https://pypi.org/simple`; never its `publish-url`) with `curl` and `Accept: application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json`. In a 200 JSON body, any matching yanked file means absent; otherwise at least one matching non-yanked file means present. That version-level read serves every use outside an effect. Before a PyPI effect, `release execute` proceeds without a build when the index has no file of the version. Otherwise it builds, and treats the release as already satisfied only when every built file is on the index by filename and not yanked. A built file the index holds yanked is a remote conflict, and a file the index holds that the build did not produce is reported with a warning and not checked. After an upload, confirmation waits for every built file to be visible, and a file this run uploaded must carry the sha256 the index serves for it, or the run fails with E307. A file from an earlier attempt is matched by name, not by digest, unless the artifact manifest seals the release's files: then the run builds nothing, uploads those exact files, compares the sha256 of every file the index holds under a sealed name, and fails with E307 before any upload when one differs. A 404 or no matching file means absent, and a non-JSON body or other non-retryable status is indeterminate. Transient HTTP statuses use the observation retry policy.

After a publish command reports success, Callisto re-observes the registry and treats "absent" as not yet propagated, retrying within the observation limit. A publish whose version the registry never shows fails with E157, including one whose output says the version already exists, and no receipt is written.

Read-only observations (registry query, GitHub release lookup, `git ls-remote`) run at most 5 attempts with exponential backoff from 2 s, capped at 300 s. HTTP 429, 5xx, rate-limited 403 and failed commands are retried, and an observation still indeterminate fails with E176 before that operation's effect.

A publish command that fails with auth, rate-limit or other registry output fails the run with E163. A failing git or gh effect command fails with E164. No effect command is re-issued automatically. Tool output shown in these errors, in the live stderr echo and in JSON errors has credentials masked as `[REDACTED]`: the values of the known credential variables and of any variable named `*_TOKEN`, `*_SECRET` or `*_PASSWORD`, URL userinfo, `npm_`, `ghp_`-family, `github_pat_` and `pypi-` tokens, `Bearer` values, and `.npmrc` `_authToken`, `_auth` and `_password` values.

A `pypi` `[registries]` entry may set `publish-url`, the endpoint Twine uploads to when the index at `url` is not also the upload route. Both endpoints follow the registry URL rules of REL-PUB-05 and both enter the registry binding, so changing either makes an earlier intent stale. A package-level `publish-to` index names both routes and overrides the entry's `publish-url`. A `publish-url` on a registry that is not `pypi` is rejected when the configuration loads.

An operation whose result is already present and identical is recorded as already satisfied, and its effect is not repeated. For a registry version, stderr shows `warning: <package> <version> is already published; skipping`. During `release execute`, a Python release is satisfied only when every file its build produces is on the index, so a rerun after a partial upload uploads only the missing files. The check that finds a tagged package still to finish reads the version-level answer and does not build.

After a run fails partway, rerunning the same command with no state file from the failed run performs only the missing operations and writes a receipt. A local annotated tag on the expected commit that is missing on the remote is pushed before the receipt is written, regardless of its annotation text. `Nothing to release.` is reported only when every operation of every package tagged on the current commit is observed already satisfied. A failure to read the local tag state other than the tag being missing stops the run with an error before any effect.

Any of these fails with E167 and is never adopted: a local or remote tag on another commit, a lightweight tag, a GitHub release with a different prerelease flag, an asset of the same name with a different size or sha256, or two assets with the same name. A tag's identity is its target commit plus being annotated; annotation text is never compared.

A receipt is written only when every operation ends `published` or `alreadySatisfied`, and otherwise the run exits 1 with no receipt file (E172 when operations remain incomplete). The receipt records `intentDigest`, the envelope (`orchestrationRevision`, `releaseSourceRevision`, intent and artifact-manifest digests), and each operation's outcome and provider evidence.

`workflow_dispatch` with `release_source_sha` releases that commit using the current workflow run's commit as the orchestration revision. The SHA must be 40 lowercase hex characters, resolve to that same commit, and be a GitHub-verified commit merged into `main` from `callisto/version-packages` or `callisto/version-packages--<40-hex>` in the same repository. A recovery run skips `verify` and `version-pr` and is gated by `recovery-checks`.
A tag push that GitHub refuses because the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip fails with E180, naming the tag and target commit.
Every package with a publish target gets an annotated, unsigned tag named by its tag template, with message `Release <tag>`, on the source commit, pushed to the `origin` push URL.

A package that targets `github-release` gets `gh release create <tag> --repo <owner/repo> --verify-tag --draft`, adding `--prerelease` for prerelease versions. After all its assets upload, the release is published with `gh release edit <tag> --draft=false`.

Release notes are the body of the package CHANGELOG section for the version, passed with `--notes-file`. With no changelog configured, a missing file, or a missing or empty section, Callisto passes `--generate-notes` and prints `notes: using generated notes (<reason>) for <package>` to stderr. A changelog that exists but cannot be read (a permission error, a directory, bytes that are not UTF-8) fails release planning with E125 naming the file, because generated notes would silently replace what the release PR reviewed.

Each `[[release.artifact]]` becomes one upload named `asset-name` on the product package's GitHub release, tagged with the product's own tag and prerelease flag regardless of the asset owner package's version. An artifact whose `package` is not in the release fails with E179, and a `product-package` that is missing or does not target `github-release` fails with E197. When an artifact's owner package is selected but the product package is not, Callisto warns on stderr, records a `product-artifact-owner-without-product` diagnostic (surfaced in `--format json`; see REL-CMD-04), and derives no slot for that asset.

`release artifact-manifest` requires, for each slot, a regular non-symlink file named `asset-name` directly in `--artifact-dir` (`E221` for a symlink or non-file, an I/O error when missing) and records its sha256 and byte length. With slots, `release execute` requires both `--artifact-manifest` and `--artifact-dir` (`E233`); without slots it rejects either flag (`E232`) unless the manifest seals Python files. `--seal-python` records the wheel and sdist of every Python publish of the plan, sealed all or none, each named for its package and version, and `release execute` verifies each file's sha256 and byte length (`E139`) before any effect.

Before any effect, `release execute` fails with E139 when an artifact's bytes differ from the manifest. It fails with E140 unless `gh attestation verify` passes with the configured `--repo`, `--signer-workflow <repo>/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, `--signer-digest` set to the orchestration revision, `--source-digest` and `--deny-self-hosted-runners`.

In the release workflow, `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` reaches only the `execute` job's execute step. The workflow's default permissions are empty, and the plan and build jobs receive no registry credential.

Callisto finds a GitHub release by tag, draft or published, with the GraphQL `release(tagName:)` lookup followed by `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/{id}`; it never reads the release list. After its own release create, asset upload or publish, a release or asset still absent is looked up again with 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s and 32s waits before the run fails with E167.

`release-pr decide` returns `noop` when there are no pending changesets. It returns `update` when one open PR from the same repository has head `<release-branch>` or `<release-branch>--<40 lowercase hex>`, and `create` otherwise.

`release-pr decide` fails in these cases: pre mode (E318, because a release PR cannot consume the changesets pre mode keeps), an invalid repository (E141), an unsafe branch name (E142), duplicate PR numbers (E143), a snapshot for another repository or base branch (E144), a managed-branch PR from a fork (E145), more than one managed PR (E146), a malformed SHA suffix (E147), or a PR headed at `<release-branch>--staging` (E154). Each of these carries its own code even when `--snapshot`/`--decision` is a file, inline JSON, or stdin. `release-pr verify` accepts either the bare decision wire or unchanged `release-pr decide --format json` output through all three input forms. Report metadata, when present, contains both `command: release-pr decide` and boolean `dryRun`; unknown or duplicate fields and malformed, partial or null metadata fail with E281. Nested domain validation retains its typed diagnostic. Verification exits 0 when a fresh snapshot equals the decision's snapshot and fails with E148 otherwise.

`release-pr commit-plan` resolves the repository root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so it works from any subdirectory of the checkout, and emits base64 additions and deletions for the index staged against `--base-commit`. Each added or modified file's content is verified against the index blob sha before it is emitted; a worktree file edited again after staging fails the read (E059) rather than emitting content that does not match what is staged. It fails for: no changes (E149); a mode other than 100644 (E150); a type change or unmerged path (E151); over 4 MiB of content (E152); or a path under `.github/workflows/` or `.git/`, an absolute path, or one containing `..` (E153).

The release-PR action runs the version command with `--emit-decision <decision_path>` (default `.callisto/release-decision.json`). It commits the result with GitHub's `createCommitOnBranch` on `<release-branch>--staging` reset to the base commit, and refuses unless the remote tree equals the locally staged tree. It then moves the release branch ref through the REST API and never runs `git push`. Before creating the commit, before moving the ref, and before any label or PR write, it runs `callisto release-pr verify` against a fresh snapshot and stops when verification fails. After an update ref move is read back successfully, the final check supplies `--applied-head <new_sha>`. This accepts only a consistent update decision's selected PR changing to that exact head; any other snapshot change, wrong applied head, or create/noop use fails E148. The final check is retried for up to 27 seconds while the PR list still shows the old head, because the forge can lag a ref move; a head that never shows the applied commit still fails E148. Checks before the move and the create path retain strict original-snapshot equality.

`callisto-action` with `mode: release` runs `callisto --format json release --receipt <tmp>` and sets `published` and `publishedPackages` from registry and platform publish operations whose outcome is `published`. A `mode` other than `version-pr` or `release` fails the step.

With `source: auto`, `callisto-action` and `setup-callisto` default `version` input `latest` installs the callisto release the action's own invocation is pinned to (`github.action_ref` resolved against `orin-dx/callisto`'s `callisto@` tags), falling back to the newest published release only when that ref is unset or matches no tag. An explicit `version` input overrides this resolution, including inside a Callisto checkout. A consumer manifest mentioning callisto-cli never selects a local build. `source: local` ignores version pins and requires Git-tracked Callisto source at the checkout root plus Cargo metadata confirming the local callisto-cli workspace member, manifest path and callisto binary target. Local builds use explicit manifest and output-directory paths; invalid local source fails without falling back to a downloaded or registry installation.

`--format json` output of `release-pr verify`, `release-pr decide` and `release-pr commit-plan` (without `--out`) goes through the same envelope every other command's JSON report uses: a top-level `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun`, alongside that subcommand's own payload fields unchanged. `release-pr verify --decision` accepts `release-pr decide --format json` output as-is.
Every release failure exits 1 with a diagnostic carrying an `E####` code.
`--dry-run` with `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest` or `release execute` fails with `E217`, `E216` or `E218` and writes nothing.

A `[release]` section fails config loading with E197 when it has no `[[release.artifact]]`, an unqualified `product-package` or artifact `package`, an unsafe `target` or `asset-name`, or a duplicate `asset-name`. It also fails for a `[release.profiles.<name>]` other than `production`, or a `production` forge-repository that conflicts with the top-level key.
